questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to be in Europe and experience other cultures while expanding my social network.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the academic experience on exchange to be far more exciting than anticipated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Just fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An introduction letter.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was horrible and stressful. I found a place were I got some great roommates, but the whole process to get there was bad. I had a bad landlord, and a friend of mine had to move out because hers was crazy. It's just exhausting and not the kind of things you want to worry about while abroad.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That the housing situtation is bad, and you may have to go on FaceBook, so look out for scammers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The motivational letter was just fine, but signing up for courses was a bit stressful with first-to-princip, and the website was lacky, so just a bit uncool. But hey, it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, I guess the administration for exchanges?

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready in time, and have other priorities ready in case the ones you want are unavailable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were great, and the workload was perfect.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was MUCH more engaged while abroad. The teaching was more immersive and interesting, and the encouragement of creativity and innovation in e.g. the grading rubrics really nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Creativity and Innovation in Contemporary Business (CM2085), Diversity in Popular Culture and Advertising (CM2076), Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Media and Creative
Industries (CM2079), Management and Leadership in Media Organizations (CM2078), Digital Content (CM2011), Feeling Orange

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Management and Leadership in Media Organizations (CM2078) and Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Media and Creative
Industries (CM2079) were the best! The teacher is passionate and sweet, the workload is perfect as an exchange, and the exams are interesting and not as stressful as at UCPH.

questions.answer: Having to pay (quite a lot) to be a part of the introduction activities.

questions.answer: Introduction, fitness, bike were all more expensive.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At uni there is a nice fitness where you can take different classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The classes at fitness, ESN tuesdays, cantus

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel with friends to nearby cities on day trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, it's a lot like Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nope, they're not much into talking with people who don't speak their language.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I have been harassed more in public in the Netherlands than I've ever been at home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The innovational mindset.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The international community is great (and everyone speaks English!), be ready for the housing challenge, and have fun:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Housing shortage, everything is expensive, rent a bike!, get a rain coat

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got really interested and into academics again, which was nice, since I felt a bit drained at UCPH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The locals and their hostility towards outsiders.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
